# antigravity.google documentation — Docs — Ide

> 23 page(s) of antigravity.google documentation — Docs under Ide. Part of the index one level up (../llms.txt).

## Ide

- [overview](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/overview/): AI-powered IDE
- [Getting Started](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/getting-started/): Please visit [antigravity.google/download](https://antigravity.google/download) to download Antigravity IDE.
- [Supported IDEs & Editors](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/extensions/): Antigravity uses a unified authentication system across all IDE extensions, the Antigravity CLI, and Antigravity 2.0 (Desktop).
- [Prerequisites](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/extensions/vscode/): 1. Open Visual Studio Code.
- [Prerequisites](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/extensions/visual-studio/): 1. Open Visual Studio 2026.
- [jetbrains](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/extensions/jetbrains/): Antigravity supports the full suite of **IntelliJ-based IDEs**—including IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, CLion, Rider, and more—starting with version **2026.2.1+**.
- [Prerequisites](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/extensions/zed/): 1. Open Zed.
- [xcode](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/extensions/xcode/): You can now access Antigravity directly inside Apple’s **Xcode** to build across Apple platforms (including macOS, iOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and visionOS) without leaving your native…
- [Antigravity IDE: Tab & Navigation](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/tab/): This guide covers the core navigation and completion tools: **Supercomplete**, **Tab-to-Jump**, and **Tab-to-Import**.
- [Agent Side Panel](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/agent-side-panel/): Use the panel on the right side of the editor to work directly with the agent.
- [Review Changes](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/review-changes-editor/): Once the agent has begun writing code within a conversation, you’ll see a `Review Changes` section within the Agent panel’s [bottom…
- [Implementation Plan](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/implementation-plan/): Agent utilizes the implementation plan artifact to architect changes within your codebase to accomplish a task.
- [Walkthrough](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/walkthrough/): Agent creates walkthrough artifacts when it has completed task implementation; this type of artifact includes a concise summary of the changes that have been made to remind the…
- [browser](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/browser/): Allowlist & Denylist
- [Allowlist / Denylist](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/allowlist-denylist/): The browser uses a two-layer security system to control which URLs can be accessed: - **Denylist** - Deny dangerous/malicious URLs - **Allowlist** - Explicitly allow trusted URLs
- [Separate Chrome Profile](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/separate-chrome-profile/): To isolate the browser from your general browsing, it operates on a [separate Chrome profile](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/2364824).
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/mcp/): Antigravity supports the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), an open standard that lets AI agents and editors securely connect to local developer…
- [Agent Skills](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/skills/): Skills are an [open standard](https://agentskills.io/home) for extending agent capabilities.
- [Global Rules](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/rules/): Global rules live in ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md and are applied across all workspaces.
- [Workflows](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/workflows/): Workflows enable you to define a series of steps to guide the Agent through a repetitive set of tasks, such as deploying a service or responding to PR comments.
- [Plugins](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/plugins/): Plugins are namespaced bundles that allow you to extend Antigravity’s capabilities by grouping skills, rules, MCP servers, and hooks into a single package.
- [Configuration](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/hooks/): Hooks are configured in a `hooks.json` file located in your customization directory (e.g., `.agents/` in your workspace or `~/.gemini/config/`).
- [Settings](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/settings/): Configure how the Antigravity Agent interacts with your environment, executes commands, and secures your workspace.
